events.text: The Heinkel He 178, the first aircraft to fly on turbojet power, makes its maiden flight
The Wright Flyer makes the first sustained powered flight at Kitty Hawk
Concorde, the Anglo-French supersonic airliner, makes its first flight from Toulouse
Charles Lindbergh flies solo and nonstop from New York to Paris

reveal.explanation: Powered flight began on a windswept beach in North Carolina, and within a single lifetime passengers were crossing the Atlantic faster than sound. The jet age arrived quietly in 1939 with a six-minute test flight in Germany, only twelve years after Lindbergh's piston-engined Atlantic crossing.

sources.excerpt: The Wright Flyer (also known as the Kitty Hawk, Flyer I or the 1903 Flyer) made the first sustained flight by a manned heavier-than-air powered and controlled aircraft on December 17, 1903.
On May 20–21, 1927, he made the first nonstop flight from New York to Paris, a distance of 3,600 miles (5,800 km), flying alone for over 33 hours.
On 27 August 1939, the He 178 V1, the first prototype, performed its maiden flight, piloted by Erich Warsitz.
Construction of six prototypes began in February 1965, with the first flight from Toulouse on 2 March 1969.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: Concorde's UK-built prototype flew on 9 April 1969 and the type entered service in 1976, but the article gives 2 March 1969 as the first flight; the He 178 made a short hop three days before its 27 August 1939 maiden flight, same year either way; Lindbergh's flight is dated 20–21 May 1927, the same year; the Wright Flyer date of 17 December 1903 is stated without hedging.
